paragraphs: Rep'd describes itself as the AI communications platform for local government. The platform offers short video messages that staff send to residents, with built-in CRM tools and email templates. Residents submit questions, and typeahead suggestions route them to answers that already exist.

Recording runs through a teleprompter mode meant for one take. A question can be shared with any staff member, which the site presents as a way to highlight experts on staff. The pages also list a real-time analytics dashboard for seeing what residents care about. A social media management suite is listed for creating, sharing and tracking posts.

Rep'd was built by Mike Baumwoll and Mark Friese, who worked together at Twitter. The founders describe the product as an AI-powered video chatbot that humanizes local government. Officials quoted in the case studies include a city manager and a mayor.

quote.text: Rep'd is built on the belief that vibrant, trusting communities are created not through anonymous posts or walls of text, but by enabling real people-names, faces, and voices-to engage directly, honestly, and respectfully.
